rounds.text: Thangamayil Jewellery demonstrates exceptional operational efficiency, evidenced by a Return on Equity of 28.1% [E13] and a Return on Capital Employed of 25.5% [E12], both of which significantly outperform their respective sector benchmarks [E9, E10]. This profitability is supported by explosive growth, with compounded sales growth reaching 83% and profit growth hitting 264% over the trailing twelve months [E17, E21]. Institutional confidence is clearly rising, as evidenced by the shift in holdings from 0.25% to 5.54% for foreign institutions and 11.39% to 16.43% for domestic institutions since September 2023 [E42, E43]. The company operates within a sector currently experiencing a positive tailwind [E73, E75], and its relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 confirms its status as a market leader [E51]. Conceded: the stock trades at a high price-to-book ratio of 12.06x compared to the sector benchmark of 2.08x [E7], and the promoter holding has decreased by 5.55 percentage points over the last three years [E41, E65]. Despite these valuation concerns, the company’s ability to generate Rs 249 Cr in free cash flow as of March 2026 underscores a robust underlying business model [E36].

Thangamayil Jewellery is currently trading at a significant premium, with a price-to-book ratio of 11.84x compared to a sector benchmark of just 2.08x [E2, E7]. This valuation is further strained by a negative margin of safety of -5.3%, as the current market price of ₹ 5,397 exceeds the calculated intrinsic value of ₹ 5,126 [E45, E46]. The stock’s price has historically outpaced fundamental growth, as evidenced by a 5-year share price growth of 66% against a profit growth of 32% [E56]. Furthermore, the company’s reliance on debt is increasing, with borrowings rising to ₹ 913 Cr from ₹ 797 Cr in the prior year [E39]. There is also a concerning trend of declining promoter ownership, which has dropped by 5.55 percentage points since September 2023 [E41, E65]. Conceded: the company has demonstrated strong historical sales and profit growth, including a 264% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E17, E21]. Despite these operational successes, the current valuation already implies an aggressive earnings growth rate of 18.7%, leaving little room for error should performance decelerate [E47, E71].
